'''Alun Mark Anderson''' (born 27 May 1948) is a Welsh scientist and science journalist. He is best known as the editor in chief and publishing director of ''[[New Scientist]]'' from 1992 to 2005. He continues to act as a consultant for the magazine. In 2009 he published ''After the Ice: Life, Death, and Geopolitics in the New Arctic'', about the effects of [[climate change]] on the wildlife and native peoples of the arctic region.<ref>{{Cite book |isbn = 978-0061579073|title = After the Ice: Life, Death, and Geopolitics in the New Arctic|last1 = Anderson|first1 = Alun|date = December 2009| publisher=HarperCollins }}</ref>

A 2003 interview at the University of Sussex is the likely inspiration for [[Richard Dawkins]]' famous quote "Science is interesting and if you don't agree you can fuck off".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sussex.ac.uk/Units/alumni/notable_alumni/interviews/Anderson_interview.html |title=Interview with Alun Anderson - Editor-in-Chief of New Scientist magazine |last=Kirk |first=Simon |date=May 2003 |publisher=University of Sussex |access-date=6 May 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080226010755/http://www.sussex.ac.uk/Units/alumni/notable_alumni/interviews/Anderson_interview.html |archivedate=26 February 2008 }}</ref>
